title: Final: loading and hosting
sub: The host, runtime versions, contexts, unloading and crashes
cards/0/q: Assemble the startup of dotnet app.dll from the command to Main
cards/0/items/0: The muxer takes the newest hostfxr from host/fxr
cards/0/items/1: hostfxr reads runtimeconfig.json and picks a Microsoft.NETCore.App version
cards/0/items/2: hostpolicy from the framework folder builds the TPA from deps.json
cards/0/items/3: coreclr starts the GC and JIT and loads System.Private.CoreLib
cards/0/items/4: The default context loads app.dll, and Main is called
cards/0/explain: hostfxr picks the runtime version, not the muxer. The assembly list is ready before the CLR starts, and the default context takes assemblies from it.
cards/1/q: An app requests 8.0.0. Installed: 8.0.17, 9.0.6 and 10.0.2. runtimeconfig.json says rollForward = Major, but the service is started with DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor. Which runtime is picked?
cards/1/options/3: Startup fails: the settings contradict each other
cards/1/explain: The environment variable overrides runtimeconfig.json, and LatestMajor takes the newest version even when its own major is present. With Major from the file, 8.0.17 would be picked.
cards/1/wrong/1: That is what Major from runtimeconfig.json would decide. But DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD outranks the file.
cards/1/wrong/2: Major would take the nearest next major, and only if 8.x were missing entirely.
cards/2/q: What is true about hosting? Select all.
cards/2/options/0: DOTNET_ROOT overrides the registered install location for the apphost
cards/2/options/1: global.json affects the runtime choice for dotnet app.dll
cards/2/options/2: One process can hold both .NET 8 and .NET 9
cards/2/options/3: A self-contained app has hostfxr in the app folder
cards/2/explain: The apphost checks DOTNET_ROOT before the registry or /etc/dotnet and takes the first install found. global.json selects only the SDK. A process always has exactly one runtime.
cards/3/q: The host TPA has Newtonsoft.Json 13. A plugin loads into a PluginLoadContext with an AssemblyDependencyResolver, and its folder and plugin.deps.json have Newtonsoft.Json 12. Which version does the plugin code get?
cards/3/options/0: 12: the plugin Load found it before Default was reached
cards/3/options/1: 13: an assembly from the TPA always wins
cards/3/options/2: Both: each call gets its own
cards/3/options/3: FileLoadException: two versions of one name in the process
cards/3/explain: The active context for plugin references is the plugin own context. First its cache, then its Load: the resolver returned the path to version 12, and it was loaded into the plugin context. Default and the TPA were never reached.
cards/3/wrong/1: The TPA beats a path only inside the default context. In your own context its Load decides.
cards/3/wrong/3: Two versions in a process are fine if they are in different contexts. That is exactly what contexts are for.
cards/4/q: Create is a host method that loads the plugin into alc. After Run and the GC.Collect loop the context is alive. Which line blocks unloading?
cards/4/explain: The event of a long-lived host object stores a delegate, and the delegate references the plugin object. Through it the type, the assembly and the context are kept alive. The report string is a plain System.String and does not hold the context.
cards/5/q: A .NET 8 service crashed overnight. The UnhandledException handler logged an exception from a System.Threading.Timer callback. How do you keep such errors from bringing the service down?
cards/5/options/0: Catch exceptions inside the timer callback
cards/5/options/1: Set e.IsTerminating = false in the UnhandledException handler
cards/5/options/3: Create the timer inside a separate AssemblyLoadContext
cards/5/explain: A timer callback runs on the thread pool, and there is no handler above it. The only place the exception can be handled is the callback itself: a try/catch with logging and a decision about what to do next.
cards/5/wrong/1: IsTerminating only reports that the process is ending. The property cannot be changed, and the crash cannot be cancelled.
cards/5/wrong/2: That flag lived in the .NET Framework app.config. Modern .NET does not have it.
cards/5/wrong/3: A load context isolates assembly names, not threads or exceptions.
cards/6/q: You need one executable with the runtime inside, trimmed for size. Complete the project.
cards/6/explain: PublishSingleFile appends the assemblies to the apphost as one bundle. SelfContained puts the runtime inside, and PublishTrimmed removes unused code. Remember: assemblies from the bundle have an empty Assembly.Location.
cards/7/q: Match the symptom with its cause
cards/7/pairs/0/1: The contract is loaded into two contexts
cards/7/pairs/3/1: A strong reference from the host
cards/7/pairs/4/1: hostfxr found no version per rollForward
cards/8/q: A .NET 8 security patch is out, and the admin installed it on the server. The server runs two net8.0 apps: one framework-dependent, one self-contained. Which gets the fix after a restart?
cards/8/explain: A framework-dependent app takes the latest installed patch of its version at startup. A self-contained app carries the runtime in its own folder and is updated only by a new publish.
